svg.text: A sealed cavity: winding number 0, same UDF component, unreachable by any ball chain
2D hollow disk: Σ = outer circle (R = 9) ∪ inner circle (R = 6.5); wall 2.5 < 2W = 6, so both bands form one UDF component. W = 3, D = 0.55.
sealed cavity
winding 0, not material
udf > W here: outside the band
wall
winding 1
exterior
edge of the band, udf = W
udf = W
certified outside (dark: non-barrier; light: barrier, udf < D); green circles: a few of their balls, touching Σ
material (winding 1): uncertified, inside — correct
cavity, in the band (winding 0): uncertified, labelled inside
cavity, beyond the band: inactive
Fixpoint with the default stencil (|w| < W + D) and with the pedantic reach (|w| < 2W): the same 196 exterior points
certified (all of them); none of the 124 wall points and none of the 94 cavity band points.
Every certified ball is surface-free, so a chain of overlapping balls never crosses Σ; the cavity is on the other side of Σ from
every seed, so no stencil, schedule or promotion can reach it. The sweep therefore fills the cavity, which is the 'take the outermost'
fallback of InclusionSigningDesign.md §7 for surfaces nested closer than the band. With a wall thicker than about 2W the inner circle
would be its own UDF component, and the nesting stage (PropagateSign + even-odd rule) would make the cavity a void instead.
